newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Pioneer says has 10 pct of minimum funds.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Pioneer says has 10 pct of minimum funds.

text.p: Pioneer First, one of Russia's first new unit investment funds, said on Thursday more than 70 investors had bought units worth some 250 million roubles in all since the fund was launched 10 days ago.
Pioneer First is managed by KUIF, part of the First Voucher Fund, in which the U.S. Pioneer group acquired a 51 percent stake last year.

KUIF director Mikhail Chebotaryov told a news conference that since the fund went live on November 12, it had collected 10 percent of the minimum 2.5 billion roubles in investment required by the Federal Commission for the Securities Market.
Once the the primary offering, during which all units are offered at the same price, is completed, net asset values will be calculated.
Pioneer First, in common with the other first funds, will invest primarily in Russian Treasury bills.

Timothy Frost, director of the Pioneer Group's financial services activities in Russia, told the news conference the group planned to launch equity funds and a balanced fund and to make it possible to move between them.
Russian securities indutsry officials are keen to mobilise citizens' savings, estimated at some $20 billion and have said unit investment funds could attract up to 10 percent of this sum.
The securities market commission has laid down strict rules for the funds, which are similar to unit trusts in Britain, in a bid to restore public confidence in collective investment.
Many Russians lost their savings in unlicensed investment funds which turned out to be pyramid schemes.
